base_prompt: A candle burns down by the same amount each hour. It is twenty centimeters tall initially and fourteen centimeters tall after two hours. Explain the predicted height after five hours under this assumption. Use approximately 160 words for the response.
text: The candle’s height decreases at a constant rate because it burns down by the same amount every hour. It starts at 20 centimeters and measures 14 centimeters after two hours, so it has lost 20 − 14 = 6 centimeters during those two hours. Dividing 6 centimeters by 2 hours gives a burn rate of 3 centimeters per hour. After five hours, the total amount burned would therefore be 5 × 3 = 15 centimeters. Subtracting that total loss from the original height gives 20 − 15 = 5 centimeters. Equivalently, the height follows the linear rule h = 20 − 3t, where h is height in centimeters and t is time in hours. Substituting t = 5 gives h = 20 − 3(5) = 5. Thus, under the uniform-burning assumption, the predicted height after five hours is 5 centimeters.
